summary.intent: Coordinate parallel subagent workers to land a batch of cleanup and fix PRs in the caliper-docgen repo (Storybook meta forms, dependency read errors, removal of unused core API), then start a second batch covering output-contract cleanup, a tsc-client InvalidJson fix, and a scoping ADR.
summary.outcome: Three draft PRs (#371, #372, #373) were opened, had bodies written, and were merged by the user. Batch 2 was launched with three workers on separate branches under new trails #243 and #244, with no results yet.

repo: Work is tracked via Entire trails (e.g. `entire trail link 241 ... --base main --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper`); each worker branch gets linked to a trail.
User-visible changes in crates need a `.changeset/*.md` file; `just semver` checks that breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor/major changeset.

Standard local verification is `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked`, and `just lint doc-check machete typos`, run in a clean-room worktree after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`.
Worktrees without node_modules fail snapshot and terminal_react_builtins tests (e.g. snapshot_mantine); they pass in a clean room.
Sandboxed lint runs fail because pnpm needs network access; they pass when run unsandboxed.
The Storybook fix relies on `_metaAnnotations`, which the same file already reads and overrides in three other places.

Dependency-type reads now go through `Loader::read`: unreadable files emit `Diagnostic::io_read_error` (IoError, Warning) once per file, while NotFound stays a quiet skip. The index temp file is named `tmp<pid>-<atomic counter>`.
`CollectedType` has no `PartialEq`, so tests assert with `matches!` plus an assert message.
The native-binding integration test can only run in CI's native-binding jobs, since workers' checkouts lack the binding.

code.finding: A remaining `.ok()?` site the worker reported but did not touch. The orchestrator could not match this line number to what it read.
A remaining `.ok()?` that reads the installed TypeScript's platform manifest, where a missing file is expected, so it was deliberately left as is.
`needs_type_checker` and `as_string_union_keys` were removed as unused, and the removal is covered by a minor changeset.

workflow: Subagent reports are model output, not user authority. The orchestrator verified claims itself (checked the resolver `.ok()?` site) and flagged inferences such as the unreproduced node_modules cause.
Wait for CI results by job name before calling a PR ready, and never infer lint status from tail output without an exit status.
Hold dependent or overlapping branches (type-only imports, tag re-scan) until earlier PRs merge to avoid conflicts.
Tests that replace calls to removed helpers cannot be shown failing on pre-fix source. State this in the PR body.

friction: Workers read only the tail of lint output and never checked its exit status, so lint status stayed unverified until CI ran.
Unexplained CLI `commands` test failures (watch tests timing out at 30s) in the remove-unused-api worker's own worktree; a later run passed and the cause was never diagnosed.
Nine snapshot tests failed in the dependency-read-errors worker's own worktree; the missing node_modules explanation was not reproduced on main.
The sandboxed lint run failed for lack of network access.
Earlier merge conflicts led to serializing the larger cleanup behind the first batch.

Held until batch 2 merges: the type-only imports change (depends on the scoping ADR), the SPEC/AC tag re-scan, and the `benchmarks.md` banner.

Revisit the `.ok()?` site at dependency_types.rs:1216 whose line number didn't match.
